Based on the above requirements, six rules for granular filter design are recommended

Stability - The pores in the filter must be small enough to
prevent excessive migration of the base soil being drained.
As discussed in Section 5.1.2(1), the common filter design
rule of limiting the D,;F/D,;S to 5 is appropriate. As an
additional measure against failure, the filter should not be
gap-graded to prevent the loss of fine particles from the
filter itself.

Permeability - The filter must be sufficiently more
permeable than the material being drained. This
requirement would be satisfied by limiting the D,;F/D,;S
ratio to at least 5 as discussed in Section 5.1.2(2). The
presence of fine particles in significant quantities could also
influence the permeability of the filter. Hence the amount
of particles finer than 63 pm should not exceed 5% as
discussed in Section 5.1.2(3); the particle size of 63 4m has
been chosen to correspond to the BS sieve size nearest to
75 um. The filter should also be cohesionless to prevent
the formation of shrinkage cracks in the filter as a result of

drying.

Segregation - The filter should not become segregated or
contaminated prior to, during, and after installation. As
discussed in Section 5.1.2(4), it is very difficult to prevent
segregation of the filters during placement. However, to
minimize this problem, the filter should not have a broad
grading and that the maximum size of the particles should
be limited. It is recommended that the C, value be
restricted to between 4 and 20 with the maximum size of
particles limited to 50 mm.
